raw_text: A new residue experiment was designed to test what the decoded readings capture beyond the case record. Four cases (Sutton, Washington, Cotton and Brown) are blind-decoded. Each decode is compared against its case record to find the "residue," meaning what the reading asserts that the record does not support. Readings are then matched against ten candidate cases. A key design choice is that the residue step stays blind to the candidates, so the comparison cannot be steered toward a known answer. A related question was whether the account production operator should attach to the account after the fact or be modeled through a "reopening route," the path by which an official record is later revisited and turned against its authors. Acceptance checks and the account production operator were updated to explore this.
